author: potuz
content:
There's a discussion that has been spread across different threads in this server and it looks as though I am the only one arguing against everyone else. I believe this belongs here instead of in a thread and I am happy to let it go and not die on this hill, but it is such a no-brainer to me that I am a little shock not to see more reactions on the other side of the argument. 

There has always been a chicken and egg problem between testincg, specing and deciding inclusion. To deal with this problem a new governance procedure to select EIPs for inclusion was drafted almost two years ago. Roughly we have EIPs that everyone must have already implemented (included in production code and shipped in mainnet), EIPs that everyone must implement for the next fork (those are SFI) and EIPs that are more in a Gray area that may or may not land in a fork, and those are CFI, clients are encouraged to implement these but not required to implement these. 

There is an obvious need to implement and test CFId EIPs before we can make a decision to SFI them. More than implementation the biggest bottleneck is testing. We need a framework to test CFId EIPs that not everyone may have implemented, whose spec is still in flux and that may never end up being SFId anyway. 

Those are the first two legs: governance and testing. The third leg is the spec itself. On the consensus spec we keep each past fork relatively frozen and we only back port backward compatible changes. The current spec repo is the source of truth for all past forks up to the current fork and it includes all the tests that production code aims against. That deals with the EIPs that are already included. We also keep a next-fork-branch from where clients can take testvectors for the EIPs that are specific for the next fork. 

To me it is a no brainer that we must not merge into that next-fork-branch EIPs that are not SFId and EIPs that clients aren't forced to implement.

author: potuz
content:
There are mulitple reasons to justify this. Merging non-SFId EIPs on the next-fork-branch puts the onus on every single PR writer for the specs repo on the next fork, even those of SFId EIPS that are already mandatory to be in the next fork, to keep compatibility with features that are not. Puts the onus on every client that tests their production code for the next fork to keep track of features that may not be in the fork and that they ultimately are not forced to implement at this stage, at the very least not at production code level. Most importantly, interactions with these EIPs testvectors may invalidate the actual SFId features testvectors so even test coverage is affected. From the governance perspective, puts the onus on removing a CFId feature from the repo in case it's not SFId.

Now I hear the reasons to merge CFId EIPs early for testing is that it makes it simpler to release test vectors. It is simpler also for spec maintainers to not have to deal constantly with every single branch that needs to target the next fork. And I am sympathetic and acknowledge these hassles, however, they do not justify the above. Ultimately, it should be the responsibility of the feature writers to keep them compatible with the next fork, and not everyone else to keep their own work compatible with features that aren't scheduled yet.

Ultimately I believe this is a call to be more aggressive on DFIng or SFIing features quickly so that the maintainance aspects become less of a hurdle.

author: milonite
content: the issue is gasleft() can now go up (refill when you clear a slot) and the reservoir pays state gas outside the 63/64 split. so "inner call ran out of gas → caller can't finish either" doesn't hold anymore. anything doing try/catch + refund (like LZ composers) can get its catch path forced
